Describe an ingestion configuration

Source: R/doc-ingest-run.R
gr_ingest_spec.Rd

Describe an ingestion configuration

Usage

gr_ingest_spec(
  clean = "standard",
  ocr = c("auto", "always", "never"),
  ocr_lang = "eng",
  ocr_dpi = 300,
  ocr_min_chars = 40L,
  min_chars = 20L,
  extractor = NULL,
  parallel = NULL,
  cleaner_opts = list(),
  layout = c("auto", "raw"),
  layout_opts = list(),
  ocr_trigger = c("raw_text", "after_running_lines"),
  ocr_confidence = FALSE
)

Arguments

clean

A preset name ("none", "minimal", "standard", "academic", "scan", "legacy") or a character vector of cleaner names from gr_cleaners().

ocr

"auto" (OCR pages with no text layer), "always", or "never".

ocr_lang

Tesseract language code.

ocr_dpi

Render density for PDF OCR.

ocr_min_chars

A page with fewer characters than this is treated as needing OCR under ocr = "auto". Zero or more; Inf marks every page. Anything else warns and uses 40.

min_chars

Refuse the document if less than this much text survives.

extractor

Force a specific extractor name instead of dispatching on the file extension.

parallel

Parallelise page-level OCR.

cleaner_opts

Extra options passed to individual cleaners, as a named list. The built-in cleaners read these:

references_after (0.4)

For the references cleaner (in the academic and legacy presets): a References, Bibliography or Works cited heading, on a line of its own and optionally numbered or a Markdown heading such as ## References, and not inside a fenced code block, ends the text only when it starts at or after this share of the text, so an entry in a table of contents does not cut the document. A number in [0, 1]; a value that cannot be read warns and uses 0.4. Untested: set when the cleaner was written.

header_max_chars (80)

For the headers_footers cleaner (in the scan preset): the longest line, in characters, that can be taken for a running head or foot. Untested.

header_min_repeats (3)

For headers_footers: how many times a line must recur to be taken for one. Values below 3 are read as 3, and a text of fewer than 8 lines is left alone. Untested.

layout

How a PDF page's text is put in reading order. "auto" drops running heads and feet (short lines repeated at the top or bottom of many pages), reads a page set in two columns one column after the other, and marks headings, taken from the PDF's bookmarks or recognised as a standard section name ("Introduction", "Methods" and so on), so blocks carry sections. "raw" keeps each page as pdftools lays it out. Other formats are not affected. Stored in the spec only when it is not "auto", so a default spec keeps the cache and store keys it had before the setting existed.

layout_opts

Under layout = "auto", a named list that changes how running heads and feet are found on PDF pages: depth (2, lines at each edge of a page that are candidates), share (0.4, the share of pages a line must recur on), min_pages (3, the fewest pages a document needs before any line is dropped, and the fewest a line must recur on), max_chars (200, the longest candidate line) and max_words (5, above which a numbered line must carry its number where a page number is set). Names left out keep these defaults, which were set when the PDF reader was written and are untested. An unknown name is an error. Stored in the spec only when it is not empty.

ocr_trigger

Under ocr = "auto", which of a PDF page's text ocr_min_chars is counted on. "raw_text" (the default) counts the whole text layer, as before. "after_running_lines" counts what is left once the running heads, feet and stamps that layout = "auto" drops are taken out (with layout_opts), so a scanned page whose text layer holds only a 60-character fax header or Bates stamp repeated on every page is OCR-ed. Untested.

ocr_confidence

TRUE gives each block of a PDF page that OCR read an ocr_confidence column: Tesseract's mean word confidence for the page, from 0 to 100, from a second Tesseract pass over the page. FALSE (the default) skips that pass, so OCR takes the time it did before, and the blocks have no such column. Untested.

Value

A list of class gr_ingest_spec.

Where the defaults come from

Each setting's default, its tier and the evidence behind the value, as in gr_read_spec().

  • ocr (default "auto", basic): untested. OCR only where a page has no text layer; not compared.

  • layout (default "auto", advanced): untested. The layout pass is on; checked on the PDFs in the tests, with no measured comparison against "raw".

  • clean (default "standard", basic): untested. The preset meant for born-digital text; not compared.

  • ocr_lang (default "eng", advanced): untested. English, the language of the package's own examples.

  • ocr_dpi (default 300, advanced): cited. Tesseract's documentation on improving output quality recommends images of at least 300 DPI; not measured here.

  • ocr_min_chars (default 40, advanced): untested. Set when OCR was added; not tuned.

  • min_chars (default 20, basic): untested. A floor that catches an empty extraction; not tuned.

  • extractor (default NULL, advanced): untested. Not a tuned value: NULL chooses by file type.

  • parallel (default NULL, advanced): untested. Not a tuned value: NULL follows hr_options("parallel"). It does not change output.

  • cleaner_opts (default list(), advanced): untested. Empty: each cleaner uses its own defaults, listed under cleaner_opts.

  • layout_opts (default list(), advanced): untested. Empty: the pass uses the values it was written with, listed under layout_opts; none was tuned.

  • ocr_trigger (default "raw_text", advanced): untested. "raw_text" counts the whole text layer, as before; not compared with "after_running_lines".

  • ocr_confidence (default FALSE, advanced): untested. FALSE: OCR runs one Tesseract pass per page, as before. Not compared with TRUE.

See also

gr_ingest(), gr_cleaners() for the individual step names, gr_clean() to preview a configuration on your own text

Other ingest functions: gr_clean(), gr_cleaners(), gr_document, gr_extractors(), gr_ingest(), gr_register_cleaner(), gr_register_extractor()

Examples

# What each preset costs you, on a real document, before any model call.
vapply(c("none", "minimal", "standard", "academic", "scan"),
       function(p) gr_ingest(gr_example(), gr_ingest_spec(clean = p))$stats$chars,
       integer(1))
#> Using cached ingestion for this document + settings.
#> Extracting 'annual_report.md' with the 'md' extractor.
#> Ingested 19 block(s), ~586 tokens (0 chars removed by cleaning).
#> Using cached ingestion for this document + settings.
#> Extracting 'annual_report.md' with the 'md' extractor.
#> Ingested 13 block(s), ~499 tokens (203 chars removed by cleaning).
#> Extracting 'annual_report.md' with the 'md' extractor.
#> Ingested 17 block(s), ~574 tokens (12 chars removed by cleaning).
#>     none  minimal standard academic     scan 
#>     1858     1858     1846     1655     1846 

# Or name the steps yourself; see gr_cleaners() for what is available.
gr_ingest_spec(clean = c("page_numbers", "references"), ocr = "never")$clean
#> [1] "page_numbers" "references"  

# A bibliography heading counts only in the last half of the text.
gr_ingest_spec(clean = "academic", cleaner_opts = list(references_after = 0.5))
#> $clean
#> [1] "academic"
#> 
#> $ocr
#> [1] "auto"
#> 
#> $ocr_lang
#> [1] "eng"
#> 
#> $ocr_dpi
#> [1] 300
#> 
#> $ocr_min_chars
#> [1] 40
#> 
#> $min_chars
#> [1] 20
#> 
#> $extractor
#> NULL
#> 
#> $parallel
#> NULL
#> 
#> $cleaner_opts
#> $cleaner_opts$references_after
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#>
